key_insight: PhysMiner automates turbulence-physics discovery by combining shear-free triple decomposition of velocity gradients with LLM-driven reasoning and validation.
engineering_relevance: It can improve flow diagnosis and turbulence-model development in complex engineering applications by reducing shear contamination and extracting more reliable physics signatures.
method: Triple-decomposes the velocity-gradient tensor into rigid rotation, pure shear, and normal straining.
Uses an agentic pipeline to analyze statistics, visualize structures, extract vortex lines, and infer physics from literature and flow patterns.
Adds a review agent plus an evolving knowledge library to validate conclusions and accumulate cross-case turbulence knowledge.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated across five benchmarks and end-to-end on periodic hill flow, where it autonomously proposes an improved subgrid-scale model with better Reynolds-stress predictions.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality of automated decomposition and agent reasoning, so robustness and generalization to unseen flows still need careful verification.
paper_title: PhysMiner: An Agentic AI Framework for Discovering Turbulence Physics
